spec.sequence: Leaving the track on the seep's west shore, the way climbs north beside the water; the furnace shows first at the top of the rise, then the hut beyond it.
spec.wayfinding: One way runs north from the track along the shore and up the bench; it passes the furnace floor and ends at the hut door.

spec.value: Bog iron forms itself in this ground. A road that eats iron will pay for it.
The diggers come from three villages for one season a year. They consider the work shameful.
The seep is being worked out; each season's cakes are smaller and further from the path.
A stagnant iron-rich seep where the ore can be lifted from the mud in cakes.

value.loreSource: catalogue record Bog Iron Workings (works, M1; occupants D2 seasonal diggers, few; interior a dwelling S1, one door)
value.why: A season's crew of three to six from three villages: one sleeping hut with a furnace floor beside it.

spec.orientationWhy: Its door turns east-south-east toward the furnace floor and the way from the road.

playerPurpose.note: The season's crew know which end of the seep they stopped working. They also know what took the last digger who went there (LF67).

sockets.why: Something lives in the deep end of the seep, where the water stands 1.5 m deep and the diggers have stopped working (contents c1, LF67).
Beside the hut door, where the crew leave their boots, stained orange to the knee by the seep.
The crew cooks its evening meal at its own fire on the furnace floor.
The diggers sleep in the crew's hut through their season.
The diggers feed the furnace and work the bellows through the day.
The diggers' hut door, the place's one lived-in entrance.
A crew of diggers from three villages works the seep and the furnace for one season.
The head of the bank over the seep, where the ore digger brings the cakes up.
The clay furnace, broken open each season to free the bloom.
